The notation $(f/g)(x)$ means the quotient of the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x).$

**Method 1**

To evaluate $(f/g)(2),$ we find $f(2)$ and $g(2),$ and then divide the results.

First, we find $f(2)$ and $g(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & =(2)^{2}-4=0 \\ g(2) & =2(2)+2=6\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we divide the results:

$$
(f/g)(2)=\frac{f(2)}{g(2)}=\frac{0}{6}=0
$$

**Method 2**

First, we find $(f/g)(x)$ by dividing $f$ by $g$:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f/g)(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}-4}{2x+2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate $(f/g)(2):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}(f/g)(2) & =\frac{(2)^{2}-4}{2(2)+2}=\frac{0}{6}=0\end{aligned}
$$
